subject: maths
title: Primary 6 Ratio
seo_title: P6 Ratio Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus, PSLE Practice)
standard_text: Notation and interpretation of a : b and a : b : c; equivalent ratios; simplest form; dividing a quantity in a given ratio; missing terms; relationship between fraction and ratio
meta_desc: P6 ratio practice: simplest form, missing terms, ratio and fraction, sharing in a ratio with models and PSLE-style problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A ratio 2 : 3 means 2 units and 3 units. Find 1 unit first, then multiply.
key_sub: Share $60 in the ratio 2 : 3: 5 units = $60, 1 unit = $12, so $24 and $36.
body_html:
What is a ratio?

A ratio compares two or more quantities. We write it with a colon: a : b or a : b : c. A ratio has no units.

Order matters. Write the numbers in the same order as the words. Circles to squares is 2 : 5. Squares to circles is 5 : 2.

Equivalent ratios and simplest form

Multiply or divide every term by the same number to get an equivalent ratio. A ratio is in its simplest form when the terms have no common factor except 1.

Example

Express 12 : 18 in its simplest form.

The highest common factor of 12 and 18 is 6. 12 ÷ 6 = 2 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

Answer: 2 : 3

Example

Find the missing term. 3 : 5 = 12 : ?

3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the second term by 4 too: 5 × 4 = 20.

Answer: 20

Ratio and fraction

If A : B = 2 : 3, then A is 2 units and B is 3 units. The total is 2 + 3 = 5 units.

A : B = 2 : 3Fraction
A as a fraction of the total25
B as a fraction of the total35
A as a fraction of B23
B as a fraction of A32

Dividing a quantity in a ratio

Draw a model with one box for each unit. Every unit has the same value. Find 1 unit first.

Example

Siti and Ali shared $60 in the ratio 2 : 3. How much did each of them get?

2 + 3 = 5 units. 5 units = $60, so 1 unit = $60 ÷ 5 = $12. Siti: 2 × $12 = $24. Ali: 3 × $12 = $36.

Answer: Siti $24, Ali $36

In before-and-after problems, look for what does not change: the total, one person’s amount, or the difference. Make those units the same, then compare.

Example

Wei Ming and Siti had money in the ratio 7 : 3. After Wei Ming gave Siti $20, they had the same amount. How much did Wei Ming have at first?

The total, 10 units, does not change. Equal shares are 5 units each, so Wei Ming gave 7 − 5 = 2 units. 2 units = $20, so 1 unit = $10. At first: 7 × $10 = $70.

Answer: $70

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing the ratio the wrong way roundThe first quantity named goes first: boys to girls is boys : girls
Reading A : B = 2 : 3 as “A is 23 of the total”Add the units to find the total: A is 25 of the total
Adding the same number to both terms: 3 : 5 = 6 : 8Multiply both terms: 3 : 5 = 6 : 10
Sharing $60 in 2 : 3 by working out $60 ÷ 2Add the units first: 2 + 3 = 5, so 1 unit = $12
Simplifying 2 m : 80 cm as 2 : 80Use the same unit first: 200 cm : 80 cm = 5 : 2

faq.q: What is taught in P6 ratio?
faq.a: Primary 6 students write ratios as a : b and a : b : c, find equivalent ratios and the simplest form, find missing terms, divide a quantity in a given ratio and link ratio with fractions.

faq.q: How do I explain ratio to my child?
faq.a: Use units: a ratio of 2 : 3 means 2 equal units and 3 equal units. Draw a bar model, find the value of 1 unit, then multiply.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with ratio?
faq.a: Mixing up part and whole. If boys : girls = 2 : 3, the boys are 2/3 of the girls but only 2/5 of all the children. Writing the ratio in the wrong order is the next most common mistake.

faq.q: Is ratio tested in the PSLE?
faq.a: Yes. Ratio is in the MOE Primary 6 syllabus and often appears in PSLE Paper 2 word problems, especially before-and-after questions solved with the model method.

sets.title: Writing ratios a : b and a : b : c

items.q: At the Singapore Zoo, a class counted 5 monkeys, 2 otters and 7 tortoises. What is the ratio of the number of tortoises to the number of monkeys to the number of otters?
items.e: Write the amounts in the order the question asks for them: 7, 5 and 2. The answer is 7 : 5 : 2, not 5 : 2 : 7 (the order in the first sentence).

items.q: At a hawker stall, 17 plates of chicken rice and 11 plates of laksa were sold in an hour. What is the ratio of the number of plates of laksa to the number of plates of chicken rice?
items.e: The question names laksa first, so write 11 first: 11 : 17. Do not copy the numbers in the order they appear in the sentence.

items.q: For National Day, Mr Tan bought 11 red balloons, 3 white balloons and 6 gold balloons. What is the ratio of the number of white balloons to the number of gold balloons to the number of red balloons?
items.e: Write the amounts in the order the question asks for them: 3, 6 and 11. The answer is 3 : 6 : 11, not 11 : 3 : 6 (the order in the first sentence).

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the total number of shapes?
items.e: There are 4 + 7 = 11 shapes altogether. Circles to all the shapes is 4 : 11. 4 : 7 compares circles with squares only.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of circles?
items.e: Count: 6 squares and 5 circles. Squares are named first, so 6 comes first: 6 : 5. 5 : 6 would be circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of triangles to the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count each shape: 2 triangles, 5 circles and 4 squares. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 2 : 5 : 4.

items.q: In a CCA group, there are 11 boys and 17 girls. What is the ratio of the number of girls to the number of boys?
items.e: The question names girls first, so write 17 first: 17 : 11. Do not copy the numbers in the order they appear in the sentence.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of circles?
items.e: Count: 5 squares and 3 circles. Squares are named first, so 5 comes first: 5 : 3. 3 : 5 would be circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares to the number of triangles?
items.e: Count each shape: 4 circles, 3 squares and 6 triangles. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 4 : 3 : 6.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count: 8 circles and 5 squares. Circles are named first, so 8 comes first: 8 : 5. 5 : 8 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count: 8 circles and 3 squares. Circles are named first, so 8 comes first: 8 : 3. 3 : 8 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of the total number of shapes to the number of squares?
items.e: There are 4 + 3 = 7 shapes altogether and 3 squares. The total is named first: 7 : 3.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count: 6 circles and 7 squares. Circles are named first, so 6 comes first: 6 : 7. 7 : 6 would be squares to circles.

items.q: Mdm Wong bought 3 kg of rice, 6 kg of sugar and 7 kg of flour. What is the ratio of the mass of sugar to the mass of flour to the mass of rice?
items.e: Write the amounts in the order the question asks for them: 6, 7 and 3. The answer is 6 : 7 : 3, not 3 : 6 : 7 (the order in the first sentence).

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the total number of shapes?
items.e: There are 3 + 4 = 7 shapes altogether. Circles to all the shapes is 3 : 7. 3 : 4 compares circles with squares only.

items.q: A class library has 19 storybooks and 17 comics. What is the ratio of the number of storybooks to the number of comics?
items.e: Storybooks are named first, so write 19 first: 19 : 17.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of triangles to the number of circles?
items.e: Count each shape: 3 squares, 5 triangles and 2 circles. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 3 : 5 : 2.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of circles to the number of triangles?
items.e: Count each shape: 6 squares, 4 circles and 3 triangles. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 6 : 4 : 3.

items.q: At a void deck, 13 adults and 14 children are waiting for a bus. What is the ratio of the number of children to the total number of people?
items.e: There are 13 + 14 = 27 people. Children to all the people is 14 : 27.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of triangles to the number of squares to the number of circles?
items.e: Count each shape: 5 triangles, 3 squares and 4 circles. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 5 : 3 : 4.

sets.title: Equivalent ratios, simplest form and missing terms

items.q: Express 36 : 27 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 36 and 27 is 9. Divide both terms by 9: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 and 27 ÷ 9 = 3, so the answer is 4 : 3.

items.q: Express 18 : 30 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 18 and 30 is 6. Divide both terms by 6: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5, so the answer is 3 : 5.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 3 : 5?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number: 3 × 4 = 12 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 3 : 5 = 12 : 20. Adding 4 to both terms (7 : 9) does not give an equivalent ratio.

items.q: Express 8 : 12 : 20 in its simplest form.
items.e: 4 is a factor of all three terms, and it is the largest one. Divide every term by 4: 2 : 3 : 5. Keep the terms in the same order.

items.q: Express 20 : 36 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 20 and 36 is 4. Divide both terms by 4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and 36 ÷ 4 = 9, so the answer is 5 : 9.

items.q: Find the missing term. 7 : 6 = 28 : ?
items.e: 7 × 4 = 28, so multiply the second term by 4 too: 6 × 4 = 24. Adding 21 to 6 gives 27, which does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Express 2 m : 80 cm in its simplest form.
items.e: Change to the same unit first: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 : 80 = 5 : 2 (divide both by 40). 1 : 40 comes from 2 : 80 without changing the units.

items.q: Find the missing term. 3 : 4 = ? : 24
items.e: 4 × 6 = 24, so multiply the first term by 6 too: 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q: Express 40 : 48 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 40 and 48 is 8. Divide both terms by 8: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 and 48 ÷ 8 = 6, so the answer is 5 : 6.

items.q: Express 12 : 15 : 6 in its simplest form.
items.e: 3 is a factor of all three terms, and it is the largest one. Divide every term by 3: 4 : 5 : 2. Keep the terms in the same order.

items.q: Find the missing term. 5 : 8 = ? : 32
items.e: 8 × 4 = 32, so multiply the first term by 4 too: 5 × 4 = 20.

items.q: Find the missing term. 42 : 12 = 7 : ?
items.e: 42 ÷ 6 = 7, so divide the second term by 6 too: 12 ÷ 6 = 2.

items.q: Find the missing term. 3 : 5 : 7 = 12 : ? : 28
items.e: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4, so every term is multiplied by 4. 5 × 4 = 20. 14 comes from adding 9 to 5 (12 − 3 = 9).

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 2 : 7?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number: 2 × 3 = 6 and 7 × 3 = 21, so 2 : 7 = 6 : 21. Adding 3 to both terms (5 : 10) does not give an equivalent ratio.

items.q: Find the missing term. 4 : 6 = 10 : ?
items.e: 10 is not a multiple of 4, so simplify first: 4 : 6 = 2 : 3. 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so the missing term is 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: Express 35 : 14 : 21 in its simplest form.
items.e: 7 is a factor of all three terms, and it is the largest one. Divide every term by 7: 5 : 2 : 3. Keep the terms in the same order.

items.q: Find the missing term. 9 : 5 = 72 : ?
items.e: 9 × 8 = 72, so multiply the second term by 8 too: 5 × 8 = 40. Adding 63 to 5 gives 68, which does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Find the missing term. 6 : 9 = 8 : ?
items.e: 8 is not a multiple of 6, so simplify first: 6 : 9 = 2 : 3. 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so the missing term is 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: Express 1 ℓ 200 ml : 800 ml in its simplest form.
items.e: Change to the same unit first: 1 ℓ 200 ml = 1200 ml. 1200 : 800 = 3 : 2 (divide both by 400). 1 : 4 comes from forgetting the 1 ℓ.

items.q: Express 18 : 6 : 24 in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 is a factor of all three terms, and it is the largest one. Divide every term by 6: 3 : 1 : 4. Keep the terms in the same order.

items.q: The mass of the bag of flour is 27 of the mass of the bag of rice. What is the ratio of the mass of the bag of flour to the mass of the bag of rice?
items.e: Think of the mass of the bag of rice as 7 units. Then the mass of the bag of flour is 2 units. So the ratio is 2 : 7, not 7 : 2.

items.q: The model shows the ratio of Hafiz’s stickers to Kavya’s stickers. What fraction of all the stickers does Kavya have?
items.e: Hafiz has 4 units and Kavya has 3 units, so the total is 4 + 3 = 7 units. Kavya has 3 of the 7 units: 37.

items.q: The model shows the ratio of Arjun’s stickers to Priya’s stickers. Arjun’s stickers are what fraction of Priya’s stickers?
items.e: Arjun has 5 units and Priya has 6 units. Compare Arjun with Priya only: 56. Do not use the total here.

items.q: Jun Jie has 3 times as many marbles as Wei Ming. What fraction of their marbles does Wei Ming have?
items.e: Jun Jie : Wei Ming = 3 : 1, which is 4 units in all. Wei Ming has 1 of the 4 units: 14. 13 compares Wei Ming with Jun Jie, not with the total.

items.q: In a car park, the ratio of the number of buses to the number of cars is 9 : 2. The number of cars is what fraction of the number of buses?
items.e: Cars are 2 units and buses are 9 units. The number of buses is the whole, so it goes in the denominator: 29.

items.q: In a box, 712 of the beads are red beads. The rest are blue beads. What is the ratio of the number of red beads to the number of blue beads?
items.e: 712 means 7 units out of 12. The rest are 12 − 7 = 5 units. So the ratio is 7 : 5, not 7 : 12.

items.q: In a basket, the ratio of the number of apples to the number of oranges is 8 : 3. What fraction of the fruits are apples?
items.e: There are 8 + 3 = 11 units in all. Apples are 8 of the 11 units: 811. 83 is wrong: the denominator must be the total, 11 units.

items.q: In a garden at Gardens by the Bay, the ratio of the number of roses to the number of orchids is 2 : 9. What fraction of the flowers are roses?
items.e: There are 2 + 9 = 11 units in all. Roses are 2 of the 11 units: 211. 29 is wrong: the denominator must be the total, 11 units.

items.q: The number of girls in a hall is 23 of the number of boys. What fraction of the children are girls?
items.e: Girls : boys = 2 : 3, which is 5 units in all. Girls are 2 of the 5 units: 25.

items.q: The length of the red ribbon is 58 of the length of the blue ribbon. What is the ratio of the length of the red ribbon to the length of the blue ribbon?
items.e: Think of the length of the blue ribbon as 8 units. Then the length of the red ribbon is 5 units. So the ratio is 5 : 8, not 8 : 5.

items.q: The model shows the ratio of Nurul’s stickers to Xin Yi’s stickers. What fraction of all the stickers does Xin Yi have?
items.e: Nurul has 2 units and Xin Yi has 7 units, so the total is 2 + 7 = 9 units. Xin Yi has 7 of the 9 units: 79.

items.q: At an animal shelter, the ratio of the number of cats to the number of dogs is 4 : 7. What fraction of the animals are cats?
items.e: There are 4 + 7 = 11 units in all. Cats are 4 of the 11 units: 411. 47 is wrong: the denominator must be the total, 11 units.

items.q: In a class library, the ratio of the number of fiction books to the number of non-fiction books is 2 : 5. The number of fiction books is what fraction of the number of non-fiction books?
items.e: Fiction books are 2 units and non-fiction books are 5 units. The number of non-fiction books is the whole, so it goes in the denominator: 25. Do not use the total here.

items.q: In a tank, the ratio of the number of goldfish to the number of guppies is 5 : 7. What fraction of the fish are guppies?
items.e: There are 5 + 7 = 12 units in all. Guppies are 7 of the 12 units: 712. 75 is wrong: the denominator must be the total, 12 units.

items.q: At a fruit stall, the ratio of the number of durians to the number of rambutans is 7 : 3. What fraction of the fruits are rambutans?
items.e: There are 7 + 3 = 10 units in all. Rambutans are 3 of the 10 units: 310. 37 is wrong: the denominator must be the total, 10 units.

items.q: In a choir, the ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls is 5 : 2. The number of boys is what fraction of the number of girls?
items.e: Boys are 5 units and girls are 2 units. The number of girls is the whole, so it goes in the denominator: 52. Do not use the total here.

items.q: Siti’s savings are 34 of Ali’s savings. What is the ratio of Siti’s savings to Ali’s savings?
items.e: Think of Ali’s savings as 4 units. Then Siti’s savings are 3 units. So the ratio is 3 : 4, not 4 : 3.

items.q: On a barbecue tray, the ratio of the number of chicken wings to the number of satay sticks is 5 : 4. The number of chicken wings is what fraction of the number of satay sticks?
items.e: Chicken wings are 5 units and satay sticks are 4 units. The number of satay sticks is the whole, so it goes in the denominator: 54. Do not use the total here.

items.q: In the queue for the Singapore Flyer, 79 of the people are adults. The rest are children. What is the ratio of the number of adults to the number of children?
items.e: 79 means 7 units out of 9. The rest are 9 − 7 = 2 units. So the ratio is 7 : 2, not 7 : 9.

items.q: In a pencil case, 611 of the pens are blue pens. The rest are black pens. What is the ratio of the number of black pens to the number of blue pens?
items.e: 611 means 6 units out of 11 are blue pens. The rest, 11 − 6 = 5 units, are black pens. Black pens come first, so the ratio is 5 : 6.

sets.title: Dividing a quantity in a ratio (model method)

items.q: The ratio of the number of Jun Jie’s cards to the number of Devi’s cards is 3 : 5. Devi has 8 more cards than Jun Jie. How many cards does Devi have?
items.e: Devi has 5 − 3 = 2 more units. 2 units = 8, so 1 unit = 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Jun Jie: 3 × 4 = 12. Devi: 5 × 4 = 20. Answer: 20.

items.q: The ratio of the number of Zhi Hao’s cards to the number of Wei Ming’s cards is 2 : 5. Wei Ming has 24 more cards than Zhi Hao. How many cards do they have altogether?
items.e: Wei Ming has 5 − 2 = 3 more units. 3 units = 24, so 1 unit = 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Zhi Hao: 2 × 8 = 16. Wei Ming: 5 × 8 = 40. Answer: 56.

items.q: In a car park, there are 3 times as many cars as motorcycles. There are 56 vehicles altogether. How many cars are there?
items.e: 3 times as many means cars : motorcycles = 3 : 1, which is 3 + 1 = 4 units. 1 unit = 56 ÷ 4 = 14. Cars: 3 × 14 = 42.

items.q: Jun Jie and Ahmad shared $80 in the ratio 5 : 3. How much money did Jun Jie get?
items.e: There are 5 + 3 = 8 units. 1 unit = $80 ÷ 8 = $10. Jun Jie got 5 units: 5 × $10 = $50. Do not divide $80 by 5 on its own.

items.q: Sarah and Siti shared 60 marbles in the ratio 3 : 2. How many marbles did Sarah get?
items.e: There are 3 + 2 = 5 units. 1 unit = 60 ÷ 5 = 12. Sarah got 3 units: 3 × 12 = 36. Do not divide 60 by 3 on its own.

items.q: In a swimming pool, there are 4 times as many adults as children. There are 45 people altogether. How many children are there?
items.e: 4 times as many means adults : children = 4 : 1, which is 4 + 1 = 5 units. 1 unit = 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Children: 1 unit = 9.

items.q: Chloe and Kumar shared 60 stamps in the ratio 2 : 3. How many stamps did Kumar get?
items.e: There are 2 + 3 = 5 units. 1 unit = 60 ÷ 5 = 12. Kumar got 3 units: 3 × 12 = 36. Do not divide 60 by 3 on its own.

items.q: Mei Ling, Ethan and Farah shared $135 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. How much money did Farah get?
Wei Ming, Siti and Priya shared 96 cards in the ratio 1 : 2 : 5. How many cards did Siti get?
items.e: 1 + 2 + 5 = 8 units. 1 unit = 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Siti got 2 units: 2 × 12 = 24.

items.q: Ali, Hafiz and Ahmad shared $70 in the ratio 2 : 5 : 3. How much more money did Hafiz get than Ali?
items.e: 2 + 5 + 3 = 10 units. 1 unit = $70 ÷ 10 = $7. Hafiz got 5 − 2 = 3 units more: 3 × $7 = $21.

items.q: Sarah, Farah and Arjun shared 96 cards in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How many cards did Sarah get?
items.e: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 units. 1 unit = 96 ÷ 12 = 8. Sarah got 3 units: 3 × 8 = 24.

items.q: Mei Ling and Ryan shared some beads in the ratio 4 : 3. Mei Ling got 24 beads. How many beads were there altogether?
items.e: 1 unit = 24 ÷ 4 = 6. There are 4 + 3 = 7 units altogether: 7 × 6 = 42.

items.q: Ryan and Devi shared $96 in the ratio 3 : 5. How much money did Ryan get?
items.e: There are 3 + 5 = 8 units. 1 unit = $96 ÷ 8 = $12. Ryan got 3 units: 3 × $12 = $36. Do not divide $96 by 3 on its own.

items.q: Xin Yi and Chloe shared some money in the ratio 4 : 7. Xin Yi got $16. How much money did Chloe get?
items.e: Xin Yi’s 4 units are $16, so 1 unit = $16 ÷ 4 = $4. Chloe got 7 units: 7 × $4 = $28.

items.q: The ratio of the number of Arjun’s cards to the number of Xin Yi’s cards is 3 : 7. Xin Yi has 16 more cards than Arjun. How many cards do they have altogether?
items.e: Xin Yi has 7 − 3 = 4 more units. 4 units = 16, so 1 unit = 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Arjun: 3 × 4 = 12. Xin Yi: 7 × 4 = 28. Answer: 40.

items.q: Ethan and Kumar shared some beads in the ratio 2 : 3. Ethan got 18 beads. How many beads were there altogether?
items.e: 1 unit = 18 ÷ 2 = 9. There are 2 + 3 = 5 units altogether: 5 × 9 = 45.

items.q: Raju and Hui Min shared 42 stickers in the ratio 5 : 2. How many stickers did Hui Min get?
items.e: There are 5 + 2 = 7 units. 1 unit = 42 ÷ 7 = 6. Hui Min got 2 units: 2 × 6 = 12. Do not divide 42 by 2 on its own.

items.q: Kavya and Hui Min shared some money in the ratio 3 : 4. Kavya got $12. How much money did Hui Min get?
items.e: Kavya’s 3 units are $12, so 1 unit = $12 ÷ 3 = $4. Hui Min got 4 units: 4 × $4 = $16.

items.q: The ratio of the number of Nurul’s cards to the number of Raju’s cards is 4 : 7. Raju has 12 more cards than Nurul. How many cards does Nurul have?
items.e: Raju has 7 − 4 = 3 more units. 3 units = 12, so 1 unit = 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Nurul: 4 × 4 = 16. Raju: 7 × 4 = 28. Answer: 16.

items.q: Zhi Hao and Ali shared $42 in the ratio 4 : 3. How much money did Ali get?
items.e: There are 4 + 3 = 7 units. 1 unit = $42 ÷ 7 = $6. Ali got 3 units: 3 × $6 = $18. Do not divide $42 by 3 on its own.

items.q: In a box, the ratio of the number of red beads to the number of blue beads was 2 : 5. Then 18 red beads were added. The ratio became 4 : 5. How many blue beads are there?
items.e: The blue beads do not change, so they stay at 5 units. Red went from 2 units to 4 units: 2 units = 18, so 1 unit = 9. Blue: 5 × 9 = 45. 90 uses 18 as 1 unit.

items.q: Farah and Nurul had stamps in the ratio 2 : 5. Each of them received 12 more stamps. The ratio became 1 : 2. How many stamps did Nurul have at first?
items.e: The difference stays the same. Before: 2 : 5, a difference of 3 units. After: 1 : 2 = 3 : 6, also a difference of 3 units. Farah went from 2 units to 3 units, so 1 unit = 12. Nurul at first: 5 × 12 = 60.

items.q: The ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in a hall was 4 : 5. After 20 boys left the hall, the ratio became 2 : 5. How many children were in the hall at first?
items.e: The girls do not change: 5 units. Boys went from 4 units to 2 units, so 2 units = 20 and 1 unit = 10. At first: 4 + 5 = 9 units = 90. 70 is the number of children after the boys left.

items.q: The ratio of the cost of a book to the cost of a pen is 9 : 2. The book costs $8.40 more than the pen. How much does the pen cost?
Arjun, Kavya and Sarah shared some stickers. Arjun got 14 of them. Kavya and Sarah shared the rest in the ratio 1 : 2. Sarah got 30 stickers. How many stickers were there altogether?
items.e: Kavya and Sarah: 1 + 2 = 3 units, Sarah 2 units = 30, so 1 unit = 15. The rest is 15 + 30 = 45, which is 34 of all. 14 of all = 45 ÷ 3 = 15. Altogether: 4 × 15 = 60.

items.q: The ratio of the length to the breadth of a rectangle is 5 : 3. Its perimeter is 64 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Length + breadth = 64 ÷ 2 = 32 cm = 8 units, so 1 unit = 4 cm. Length 20 cm, breadth 12 cm. Area: 20 × 12 = 240 cm². 960 cm² forgets to halve the perimeter.

items.q: The ratio of Zhi Hao’s savings to Xin Yi’s savings was 7 : 4. After Zhi Hao spent $45, they had the same amount. How much did Zhi Hao have at first?
items.e: Xin Yi’s savings do not change. Zhi Hao spent 7 − 4 = 3 units = $45, so 1 unit = $15. Zhi Hao at first: 7 × $15 = $105.

items.q: Mrs Ng mixes orange cordial and water in the ratio 2 : 9. She makes 2.2 ℓ of orange drink. How much cordial does she use?
items.e: 2.2 ℓ = 2200 ml. 2 + 9 = 11 units, so 1 unit = 2200 ÷ 11 = 200 ml. Cordial: 2 × 200 = 400 ml. 1100 ml comes from dividing 2200 by 2.

items.q: The ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in a school choir is 3 : 5. There are 24 more girls than boys. How many pupils are there in the choir?
items.e: Girls have 5 − 3 = 2 more units. 2 units = 24, so 1 unit = 12. Total: 8 units = 8 × 12 = 96.

items.q: For National Day, a class put up red, white and blue balloons in the ratio 2 : 5 : 3. There are 60 balloons. How many more white balloons than red balloons are there?
items.e: 2 + 5 + 3 = 10 units = 60, so 1 unit = 6. White has 5 − 2 = 3 more units: 3 × 6 = 18. 30 is the number of white balloons.

items.q: The ratio of Siti’s age to her mother’s age is 1 : 4. Her mother is 30 years older than Siti. In how many years’ time will the ratio of their ages be 1 : 3?
items.e: The difference in age never changes. Now: 3 units = 30, so 1 unit = 10. Siti is 10 and her mother is 40. Later: 1 : 3 has a difference of 2 units = 30, so 1 unit = 15. Siti will be 15: 15 − 10 = 5 years.

items.q: Raju, Priya and Kumar shared some money in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Kumar got $40 more than Raju. How much money did they share?
items.e: Kumar has 4 − 2 = 2 more units. 2 units = $40, so 1 unit = $20. Total: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 units = 9 × $20 = $180.

items.q: Mei Ling and Hui Min had stickers in the ratio 3 : 1. After Mei Ling gave 20 stickers to Hui Min, the ratio became 5 : 3. How many stickers did Mei Ling have at first?
items.e: The total stays the same. Make the totals equal: 3 : 1 = 6 : 2 (8 units) and 5 : 3 (8 units). Mei Ling went from 6 units to 5 units, so 1 unit = 20. At first she had 6 × 20 = 120.

items.q: Sarah’s money is 35 of Chloe’s money. They have $96 altogether. How much money does Chloe have?
items.e: Sarah : Chloe = 3 : 5, which is 8 units = $96. 1 unit = $12. Chloe: 5 × $12 = $60. $57.60 is 35 of $96, which uses the wrong whole.

items.q: Ahmad and Ryan had money in the ratio 5 : 3. After Ahmad gave Ryan $12, they had the same amount of money. How much money did Ahmad have at first?
items.e: The total stays the same: 5 + 3 = 8 units. Equal shares are 4 units each, so Ahmad gave 5 − 4 = 1 unit. 1 unit = $12. Ahmad at first: 5 × $12 = $60.

items.q: During Chinese New Year, the ratio of the number of red packets Jun Jie had to the number Wei Ming had was 4 : 3. After Jun Jie received 6 more red packets, the ratio became 2 : 1. How many red packets did they have altogether at the end?
items.e: Wei Ming’s packets do not change. Make his units equal: 4 : 3 and 2 : 1 = 6 : 3. Jun Jie went from 4 units to 6 units, so 2 units = 6 and 1 unit = 3. At the end: 6 + 3 = 9 units = 27.

items.q: The ratio of A to B is 2 : 3. The ratio of B to C is 4 : 5. What is the ratio of A to C?
items.e: Make B the same in both ratios. 2 : 3 = 8 : 12 and 4 : 5 = 12 : 15. So A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15, and A : C = 8 : 15.

items.q: In a CCA, 35 of the members are girls. There are 12 more girls than boys. How many members are there?
items.e: Girls : boys = 3 : 2. The difference is 3 − 2 = 1 unit = 12. Total: 5 units = 5 × 12 = 60. 36 is only the number of girls.

items.q: A hawker stall sold plates of chicken rice and nasi lemak in the ratio 5 : 3. It sold 84 more plates of chicken rice than nasi lemak. How many plates did it sell altogether?
items.e: 5 − 3 = 2 units = 84, so 1 unit = 42. Altogether: 8 units = 8 × 42 = 336. 672 uses 84 as 1 unit.

items.q: Some money was shared among Ethan, Chloe and Arjun in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. What fraction of the money did Chloe get?
items.e: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 units. Chloe got 4 of the 12 units: 412 = 13. 12 compares Chloe with the other two only.
